questions.text: In the earliest operating systems, the OS was just a library of functions. What was the biggest danger this created?

options.A: Any running program could read or write any other program's memory
options.B: Programs ran too slowly because the library had no scheduler
options.C: Users had to recompile the OS library for every new program written
options.D: A buggy program could corrupt the CPU's microcode and permanently damage the chip

questions.text: A running process calls `read()` to load data from disk. The disk is slow. Under multiprogramming, what should the OS do while waiting?

options.A: Leave the CPU idle until the disk request completes
options.B: Switch the CPU to another ready process
options.C: Cancel the read and retry it later in the background
options.D: Speed up the disk by pre-loading adjacent blocks

questions.text: Which of the following is a **mechanism**, not a policy?

options.A: Always run the job with the shortest remaining time first
options.B: Prefer I/O-bound jobs over CPU-bound jobs at all times
options.C: Saving and restoring CPU registers when switching processes
options.D: Give interactive users twice the CPU share of batch jobs

questions.text: Which are the three main OS responsibilities?

options.A: Virtualizing CPU and memory so each process has its own private view
options.B: Compiling programs to native machine code before they run
options.C: Managing concurrent access to shared data safely
options.D: Persisting data so it survives crashes and reboots

questions.text: `nginx` is started three times from the same binary. How many program and processes exist?

options.A: 3 programs and 1 process
options.B: 3 programs and 3 processes
options.C: 1 program and 1 process
options.D: 1 program and 3 processes

questions.text: A C++ function calls `new char[1024]`. Where in the process address space is the allocated region?

options.A: Heap
options.B: Code
options.C: Static Data
options.D: Stack

questions.text: Process P0 is running. It calls `read()` from disk. Which state transition occurs for P0?

options.A: READY → RUNNING
options.B: RUNNING → BLOCKED
options.C: BLOCKED → READY
options.D: RUNNING → READY

questions.text:
To create a new process, the OS performs these steps. Put them in the correct order:

```
P: The CPU begins executing the program's first instruction
Q: The OS loads the program's code and static data into memory
R: The OS allocates a stack and heap for the process
S: The OS assigns a PID and creates a Process Control Block
T: The OS places the process on the ready queue
```

options.A: Q → R → S → P → T
options.B: S → Q → R → T → P
options.C: S → R → Q → T → P
options.D: Q → S → R → T → P

questions.text: Process A and Process B both write to virtual address `0x1000`. What is the result?

options.A: The second write overwrites the first — virtual addresses are shared between processes
options.B: The OS blocks one write until the other process releases that address
options.C: Each write goes to a different physical location — each process has its own address space
options.D: Both writes are discarded — the OS reserves `0x1000` for kernel use

questions.text:
A timer fires while Process A is running. Put these steps in the correct order:

```
P: OS decides to switch to Process B
Q: Hardware saves A's registers to the kernel stack
R: OS loads B's saved registers and resumes B
S: Timer fires
T: CPU jumps to the OS interrupt handler
```

options.A: S → Q → T → P → R
options.B: T → S → Q → P → R
options.C: S → T → Q → R → P
options.D: Q → S → T → P → R

questions.text: During a context switch, who performs the **second** register save — saving kernel registers into A's PCB?

options.A: The hardware, at the same time it saves A's user registers
options.B: The OS software inside the context switch routine
options.C: The user process itself just before it is preempted
options.D: The disk driver once its current I/O request finishes

questions.text: Which are hidden costs of a context switch, beyond saving and restoring registers?

options.A: The CPU's data cache holds the old process's data, hurting the new process's performance
options.B: The OS must move the old process's heap to swap space to free memory
options.C: The TLB may need to be refilled for the new process's address translations
options.D: The OS must recompile the old process's code before it can resume

questions.text: Three jobs arrive at time 0: A=10s, B=10s, C=10s. FIFO order A→B→C. Average **turnaround** time?

options.A: 5s

questions.text: Jobs A=100s, B=5s, C=5s all arrive at time 0. FIFO runs A first, making B and C wait 100s. Which scheduling algorithm would most improve average turnaround time?

options.A: Round Robin with a 1s time slice
options.B: Shortest Job First
options.C: Priority Scheduling
options.D: Cooperative Scheduling

questions.text: Why can't the OS use SJF (Shortest Job First) for real processes?

options.A: The OS cannot know how long a job will run before it starts
options.B: SJF causes priority inversion between batch and interactive jobs
options.C: SJF requires special hardware support not found in standard CPUs
options.D: SJF only works correctly when all jobs arrive at exactly time 0

questions.text: Round Robin, time slice = 2s. Four jobs arrive at time 0. What is the **worst-case response time** for any single job?

options.A: 2s
options.B: 6s
options.C: 4s
options.D: 8s

questions.text: Job A uses 1ms of CPU then issues I/O. Job B uses the CPU non-stop. Both start at Q2 with a 10ms allotment. After A completes 4 I/O cycles and B has used 12ms of CPU, which job is at the highest queue?

options.A: B
options.B: Both
options.C: A
options.D: Neither

questions.text: A job enters MLFQ at Q2 (highest). Allotment = 10ms. It uses 7ms of CPU, then issues I/O. After returning from I/O, how much allotment is left at Q2?

options.A: 10ms
options.B: 7ms
options.C: 0ms
options.D: 3ms

questions.text: Every new job in MLFQ starts at the highest-priority queue. Why?

options.A: The OS assumes the job is short until CPU usage proves otherwise
options.B: New jobs are always more urgent than jobs already running
options.C: New jobs start at the top so they are guaranteed to run immediately within one time slice of arriving
options.D: Higher queues have more CPU cores available on multi-core systems

questions.text: A CPU-bound job enters MLFQ with queues Q2, Q1, Q0. Allotment = 10ms per queue. No I/O. After using 12ms of CPU, which queue is it in?

options.A: Q2
options.B: Q1
options.C: Q0
options.D: Q1

questions.text: Without periodic priority boost in MLFQ, which problem occurs?

options.A: New jobs skip Q2 and enter at Q0 directly to avoid priority gaps
options.B: I/O-bound interactive jobs gradually sink to Q0 through CPU overuse
options.C: Long-running CPU-bound jobs at Q0 may never receive CPU time
options.D: The scheduler must fully restart its queue structures on each new arrival

questions.text: Which two goals does MLFQ try to achieve simultaneously?

options.A: Give all jobs exactly equal CPU time across any time window
options.B: Good turnaround time by running shorter jobs before longer ones
options.C: Good response time for interactive and short jobs
options.D: Guarantee the longest-running job finishes before any new arrivals

questions.text: A process has BASE = 20KB and BOUNDS = 10KB. It accesses virtual address 11KB. What happens?

options.A: Physical address = 20KB + 11KB = 31KB; the access succeeds
options.B: The address wraps to 11KB − 10KB = 1KB within the region
options.C: The OS silently extends BOUNDS to 11KB and retries the access
options.D: The hardware raises a protection fault — 11KB exceeds the 10KB bounds

questions.text: The system uses base and bounds. A 48KB physical region is reserved for a process that only uses 6KB. The unused 42KB cannot be given to other processes. What is this waste called?

options.A: Internal fragmentation
options.B: External fragmentation
options.C: A page fault
options.D: A memory leak

questions.text:
The system uses segmentation. After several allocations and frees, physical memory contains:

```
[Used 6KB][Free 2KB][Used 10KB][Free 3KB][Used 8KB][Free 4KB]
```

A new segment needs 7KB. Total free = 9KB, but no single hole is large enough. What is this called?

options.A: Internal fragmentation
options.B: External fragmentation
options.C: A page fault
options.D: Memory overflow

questions.text: Segmentation gives each of code, heap, and stack its own base+bounds register pair. Compared to a single base+bounds for the whole address space, what is the key advantage?

options.A: The OS can compress unused segments using hardware bitmaps
options.B: The OS moves inactive segments to disk to free physical memory
options.C: The unused gap between heap and stack needs no physical memory
options.D: All segments always map to the same starting physical address

questions.text: In a paged system, a virtual address is split into two fields. What are they?

options.A: Segment number and byte offset within that segment
options.B: Physical Frame Number and total data size in bytes
options.C: Page directory index and a bounds register value
options.D: Virtual Page Number (VPN) and offset within the page

questions.text: A process needs exactly 9KB of memory. The system uses 4KB pages. How much physical memory is actually allocated?

options.A: 9KB
options.B: 8KB
options.C: 12KB
options.D: 16KB

questions.text: A program accesses the same 6 pages in a tight loop. After the first pass, nearly all accesses are TLB hits. Which principle explains this?

options.A: Spatial locality
options.B: Temporal locality
options.C: Sequential prefetching
options.D: Random access optimization

questions.text: The OS switches from Process A to Process B. The TLB still contains A's translations. To avoid flushing the entire TLB on every context switch, what mechanism does a modern OS use?

options.A: Copy A's TLB entries into B's page table so they can be reused
options.B: Tag each TLB entry with an Address Space ID (ASID) so A's and B's entries coexist safely
options.C: Mark all TLB entries as read-only until B validates them
options.D: Increase the TLB size so it holds all translations for all processes at once

questions.text: A process uses only 5% of its 4GB virtual address space. Why does a linear page table waste memory?

options.A: The table is stored in CPU registers which have very limited capacity
options.B: Each PTE is 64 bytes, making even small page tables enormous
options.C: The table must be duplicated in memory for each open file descriptor
options.D: Every virtual page has an entry, even pages the process never uses

questions.text: In a two-level page table, a page directory entry (PDE) has its valid bit set to 0. What does this mean?

options.A: No page table page exists for that virtual address region, all pages there are unused
options.B: That virtual region was swapped to disk and will reload when accessed
options.C: The PDE's frame number is zero, pointing to reserved OS kernel memory
options.D: The entire page directory is corrupt and the OS must rebuild it from scratch

questions.text: Which are advantages of multi-level page tables over a linear page table?

options.A: Page Table memory is only allocated for virtual regions the process actually uses
options.B: Each piece of the page table fits in one physical page — no contiguous allocation needed
options.C: TLB misses require fewer memory accesses with a multi-level table
options.D: Multi-level tables allow the page table to be stored on disk instead of in physical memory

questions.text: A TLB holds 16 entries and uses Least Recently Used (LRU) replacement. A program loops over 17 distinct pages repeatedly. What happens on each loop pass?

options.A: Only the 17th page causes misses; the first 16 stay permanently cached
options.B: Every page access misses
options.C: The OS detects the pattern and expands the TLB to 17 entries automatically
options.D: About half the accesses hit because LRU keeps some entries by chance

questions.text: Process X crashes due to a bad pointer. Process Y keeps running without interruption. Which virtual memory property makes this possible?

options.A: Efficiency
options.B: Transparency
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Temporal locality

questions.text: A user program tries to directly read a hardware device register at a privileged memory address. The system enforces kernel mode / user mode separation. What happens?

options.A: The OS grants hardware access after checking the program's privilege level
options.B: The access succeeds because all valid virtual addresses can be read by any running process
options.C: The program must first call an OS function to disable interrupts before hardware access is allowed
options.D: A protection fault is raised

questions.text: Two threads execute `counter++` concurrently on a shared variable. Thread 1 loads counter=10, then Thread 2 loads counter=10. Both add 1 and store. What is the final value of `counter`?
Thread A holds a mutex(lock) and is in its critical section. Thread B calls `lock()` on the same mutex. In a sleeping lock (mutex) implementation, what does Thread B do while waiting?

options.A: It executes the critical section in parallel with Thread A
options.B: It is suspended by the OS and added to a wait queue
options.C: It spins in a loop checking the lock flag until it becomes free
options.D: It raises a deadlock exception visible to the OS and both threads

questions.text: Appending a block to a file requires writing three structures: the data block, the inode, and the bitmap. The system crashes after only the data block is written. Why is journaling a better solution than fsck?

options.A: Journaling prevents crashes from occurring during disk write sequences
options.B: Journaling stores all three writes in duplicate so one copy always survives
options.C: Recovery only scans the journal log, not the entire disk
options.D: Journaling merges the three writes into a single atomic disk sector

questions.text: A file is identified internally by its inode number, not its filename. Where is the mapping from filename to inode number stored?

options.A: In the superblock, which stores a list of all file names and their on-disk locations in the file system
options.B: In the inode itself, as a special name field alongside file size and permissions
options.C: In the bitmap, which tracks which inodes are allocated and which are currently free
options.D: In the directory that contains the file
